title: Fit a tipped-back child's bike helmet: level it two fingers over the brows, then tighten its rear dial
instruction: Fit the helmet properly on the head form for a bike ride without touching its face or moving the head form, and let go.
context: NHTSA's guide (Easy Steps to Properly Fit a Bicycle Helmet, reproduced by Idaho EMS) sets a helmet "level on your head and low on your forehead—one or two finger-widths above your eyebrow" (not to "rock back more than two fingers above the eyebrows"), and for the ring says: "If the helmet has a universal fit ring instead of sizing pads, adjust the ring size to fit the head." Here the side and chin straps are already set at their marks and not handled, so the open rear ring is what lets the buckled shell tip back onto the crown, leaving the forehead bare. Order matters: tightened while tipped back, the band closes on the nape and clamps it there. Open, the shell rocks back when let go, and turning the dial pitches an unheld shell back too. One hand holds the front rim two fingers over the brow band; the other turns the rear dial in regrasps until the band clamps the occiput. Fit is read by ruler (15 to 35 mm) and a 10 N front-edge pull (< 5 mm lift).
setup: Station bench; positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x away from the arms, y left, z up from the bench. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. A Rayher female styrofoam head form (art. 3396700, 29 cm tall uncut, 55 cm round the forehead; US twin FloraCraft SmoothFoM RS260/6, 21 in / 53.3 cm), sawn level 2 mm below the chin (21.2 cm crown height), stands taped on the bench at (28.0, 0.0) +/- 0.5 cm facing +y (towards the left arm). An 8 mm dark band is painted across the forehead at the brow line, 10.2 cm over the bench (11.0 cm under the crown). A Decathlon B'TWIN KH 500 kids' bike helmet, size S (53 to 56 cm, 220 g, EN 1078, ref. 8737457 blue / 8737455 pink; US twin Schwinn Thrasher Child, 50 to 56 cm), sits buckled on the head (chin strap at a marked two-finger length, not handled), tipped back 13 +/- 1 deg onto the crown: front edge 4.6 cm over the brow band (14.8 cm over the bench, 12 mm rim top at 15.9 cm), rear fit dial (28 mm across) at its open stop, 6.7 cm over the bench. Start check: head on tape marks, strap on mark, dial open, ruler ~46 mm brow-to-edge, top photo. Fixed layout (object_jitter = 0); nothing varies by seed.
scoring: Read when the trial ends. Zero for the whole trial if an arm touches the head form's face (eyes, nose) or the head form moves more than 10 mm from its tape marks (both checked from the trial video, the final photo confirming the end state). Otherwise, with both grippers at least 30 mm from the helmet and the head and nothing moving for 1.0 s (20 steps): 0.0 if a ruler from the brow band's centre to the front edge's underside reads over 35 mm (tipped back: more than two finger widths) or under 15 mm (over the eyes), or the dial was not turned (from the video); 0.5 if it reads 15 to 35 mm but a luggage scale hooked under the front edge's centre and pulled up to 10 N lifts the edge 5 mm or more; 1.0 if it reads 15 to 35 mm and the 10 N pull lifts it less than 5 mm, held 1.0 s after both hands let go. The simulator reads the same pull from the band: a press of 24 N or more gives a friction hold of 1.38 N m, above the pull's 1.19 N m (10 N at the 115 mm front edge plus the 0.04 N m rocking back).
reset_notes: Turn the rear dial back by hand past its pawl to the open stop until the band is slack, let the helmet rock back onto the crown to its rear stop (front edge ~46 mm above the brow band), verify the chin strap sits buckled on its mark and the head form sits inside its tape marks, and check the top-camera frame; about 1 minute. Nothing is consumed, sharp, hot or wet.
fidelity: Serial chain on the taped head form (fixed to the bench): tilt hinge at the ear-strap anchors, ratchet dial (0.03 N m + band load to tighten; 0.24 N m by hand to loosen) and rear band slide (0.33 mm/click) pressing occiput and nape spheres to hold tilt by friction; chin strap at a fixed mark. Sizes and masses from maker/retailer pages; start tilt, torques, band travel and clamp force are estimates (README). Not modelled: yaw twist, foam squish, strap stretch.
